test_title: PYST 72: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: How can you identify a concave and a convex mirror based on the direction of their reflecting surfaces?

options.text: A concave mirror reflects light outward, while a convex mirror reflects it inward.
Both concave and convex mirrors have the same reflecting surface direction.
A concave mirror and a convex mirror both reflect inward.
A concave mirror has its reflecting surface curved inward; a convex mirror has its reflecting surface curved outward.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A concave mirror has its reflecting surface curved inward; a convex mirror has its reflecting surface curved outward.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **spherical mirror** is a mirror whose reflecting surface is a part of a hollow sphere of glass. Based on the direction of the curvature of the reflecting surface, they are classified into **concave** and **convex** mirrors.
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror whose **reflecting surface is curved inward**, facing towards the **center of the sphere**. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges parallel rays of light after reflection. ***Hence, statement 4 regarding the concave mirror is correct.***
 
• A **convex mirror** is a spherical mirror whose **reflecting surface is curved outward**, facing away from the center of the sphere. It is also known as a **diverging mirror** because it diverges parallel rays of light after reflection. ***Hence, statement 4 regarding the convex mirror is correct.***
 
• Statement 1 suggests a concave mirror reflects light outward; this is incorrect as concave mirrors are **converging**. Statement 2 claims both have the same direction, which is incorrect as they are **opposites**. Statement 3 claims both reflect inward, which is false for **convex mirrors**. ***Hence, statements 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• The identification of these mirrors is fundamental in **optics** for determining the nature of images (real or virtual) and their magnification levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• They are commonly used as **shaving mirrors** or **makeup mirrors** because they can produce an **enlarged and erect image** when the object is placed close.
 
• They are used in **car headlights** and **searchlights** to produce a powerful **parallel beam** of light.
 
• **Dentists** use concave mirrors to see large images of the teeth of patients.
 
• Large concave mirrors are used in **solar furnaces** to focus sunlight for heating purposes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• They are primarily used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they always give an **erect (upright) image**, although diminished.
 
• Convex mirrors provide a much **wider field of view** as they are curved outwards, allowing the driver to see a larger area of traffic behind them compared to a plane mirror.
 
• They are used as **security mirrors** in shops and automated teller machines (ATMs) to monitor large areas.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation Characteristics:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** can form both **real and inverted** images as well as **virtual and erect** images depending on the position of the object relative to the **focal point**.
 
• **Convex mirrors** always form a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image, regardless of the distance between the object and the mirror.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Principal Terminology:**
 
 
• The center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the **Pole (P)**.
 
• The center of the hollow sphere of which the mirror is a part is the **Center of Curvature (C)**.
 
• The distance between the Pole and the Center of Curvature is the **Radius of Curvature (R)**.
 
• The **Principal Focus (F)** is the point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis meet (or appear to meet) after reflection.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Relationship:** For spherical mirrors of small apertures, the **Radius of Curvature (R)** is found to be **twice the focal length (f)**, represented by the formula **R = 2f**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the focal length of a **concave mirror is negative**, while the focal length of a **convex mirror is positive**.
